about.title: Atascadero Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Atascadero's roads carry a mix of local traffic and travelers moving through on US-101, and public crash records show injury collisions happen with some regularity here, particularly around Friday afternoons when commuter and weekend traffic overlap on El Camino Real and Morro Road. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters often move fast, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor or understood the full extent of what happened to your body. Our team reviews the details of your crash, helps preserve evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness accounts, and explains your options under California law. We offer a free case review with no obligation, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurance Company

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road agency — is involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you — even if that determination is made based on something you said to an adjuster. We can help make sure your side of the story is presented accurately.

items.title: No Cap Means the Details Matter
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but proving those losses takes documentation and evidence gathered early. We can help preserve what's needed before it disappears.

items.question: Should I give the insurance company a recorded statement after my accident?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Atascadero?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's best to have your situation reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the crash happened on US-101 or Morro Road and fault is unclear?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you're partially at fault, though your compensation may be reduced accordingly. Corridors like US-101 and Morro Road see a range of crash types, so we can help gather evidence — witness statements, traffic camera footage, or police reports — to clarify what happened.

items.question: Do you charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review with no cost to you. We work on contingency, which means we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
